messages.subject: Release of seewave 2.1.0
messages.body_plain:
Dear seewave users,

A new version of seewave (2.1.0) is on CRAN now.
Many thanks to David Pinaud, Morgane Papin, Amandine Gasc, George Zhang, Glenn Seeholzer and Dan Ridley-Ellis .
Enjoy
Jerome

------

NEW FUNCTION
    o dynspectro(): a new function to dynamically explore the spectrogram of a wave with a time slider. Thanks to David Pinaud.

NEW ARGUMENTS
    o corenv(): a new argument 'ssmooth' for using a sum smooth on the amplitude envelope.
    o dynspec(): a new argument 'tlab' to control the title of the time axis.
    o fir(), ffilter(): a new argument 'rescale' to rescale the sample values of the ouput according to the sample values of the input.
    o ffilter(): a new argument 'listen' to listen to the output.
    o meanspec(): a new argument 'FUN' to control the mathematical function to be applied on the STFT rows. For instance, this argument could be set to 'median' to obtain a median spectrum rather than a mean spectrum.

OTHER CHANGES
    o now handles the class 'sound' of the package phonTools.
    o ACI(): bug regarding 'wl' fixed thanks to Del Bohnenstiehl ; bug fixed when silence occurs thanks to Morgane Papin and Amandine Gasc.
    o fir(): better localisation of the cutoff frequencies.
    o notefreq(): a small bug related to input fixed.
    o NDSI(): a bug fixed when anthropophony!=1. Thanks to George Zhang.
    o savewav(): a new argument '...' for controlling writeWave() arguments in particular 'extensible'. Thanks to Glenn Seeholzer.
    o spec(): now can handle signals of FFT window of even or odd length. Thanks to Dan Ridley-Ellis.
    o stft(): renamed stdft() due to a conflit with the stft C object. Required by CRAN checks.
    o timer(): a new stop error message when there is no signal/pause event to detect. Thanks to George Zhang.

messages.subject: Wrong frequency when using "cutw"
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I wonder if you could help. I am analysing bee buzzes, and noticed that when I read the data, the time seems to be stretched:

sdat<-readWave(filename="170914-003.wav", from=26, to=35, units="seconds")

The summary of sdat shows a duration of 9 seconds, and the file sounds fine. But when I plot an oscillogram, the x-axis stretches the data to 20 seconds:

oscillo(sdat, f=22050, from=0,  k=2, j=2, byrow=T)

Similarly, when I extract part of this Wave file using the function "cutw" the output has the wrong frequency (pitch), and I suspect this is because the time axis is interpreted wrong causing a distortion of the sound and a drop in frequency, which can be easily heard by using "play(sdat2)"

The command I used is:

sdat2 <- cutw(sdat, f=22050, from=1, to=15, plot=T, output="Wave")

Thanks,

Mario
